sanskrit: tasya rūpaṃ śarasyāsīd dhanurjyāmaṇḍalāntare dyotato bhāskarasyeva ghanānte pariveśinaḥ
english: The form of that arrow, set within the circle of the bowstring, shone like the blazing sun ringed with a halo at the breaking of the clouds.

sanskrit: pārṣatena parāmṛṣṭaṃ jvalantam iva tad dhanuḥ antakālam iva prāptaṃ menire vīkṣya sainikāḥ
english: When the son of Pṛṣata grasped that bow, it seemed to blaze; and the soldiers, beholding it, deemed that their final hour had come.

sanskrit: tam iṣuṃ saṃhitaṃ tena bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān dṛṣṭvāmanyata dehasya kālaparyāyam āgatam
english: Seeing that arrow fitted to the string by him, the mighty son of Bharadvāja judged that the appointed turn of his body's end had come.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa yatnam ātiṣṭhad ācāryas tasya vāraṇe na cāsyāstrāṇi rājendra prādurāsan mahātmanaḥ
english: Then, O lord of kings, the teacher set himself to ward off that shaft, yet the celestial weapons of the great-souled one would not come forth.

sanskrit: tasya tv ahāni catvāri kṣapā caikāsyato gatā tasya cāhnas tribhāgena kṣayaṃ jagmuḥ patatriṇaḥ
english: For four days and one night his weapons had served him without fail, but by a third part of that day his winged shafts ran out.

sanskrit: sa śarakṣayam āsādya putraśokena cārditaḥ vividhānāṃ ca divyānām astrāṇām aprasannatām
english: His arrows spent, afflicted by grief for his son, and finding the manifold celestial weapons no longer favorable to him—

sanskrit: utsraṣṭukāmaḥ śastrāṇi vipravākyābhicoditaḥ tejasā preryamāṇaś ca yuyudhe so 'timānuṣam
english: —wishing to lay down his arms, urged on by the words of the brāhmaṇas, yet driven still by his own splendor, he fought on more than mortally.

sanskrit: athānyat sa samādāya divyam āṅgirasaṃ dhanuḥ śarāṃś ca brahmadaṇḍābhān dhṛṣṭadyumnam ayodhayat
english: Then, taking up another celestial bow, that of the Aṅgirases, and arrows like the rod of Brahmā, he gave battle to Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ śaravarṣeṇa mahatā samavākirat vyaśātayac ca saṃkruddho dhṛṣṭadyumnam amarṣaṇaḥ
english: Then with a great rain of arrows he overwhelmed him, and the wrathful, unforgiving one beat Dhṛṣṭadyumna back.

sanskrit: taṃ śaraṃ śatadhā cāsya droṇaś ciccheda sāyakaiḥ dhvajaṃ dhanuś ca niśitaiḥ sārathiṃ cāpy apātayat
english: Droṇa cut that arrow of his into a hundred pieces with his shafts, and with keen darts he felled his banner, his bow, and his charioteer as well.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ prahasyānyat punar ādāya kārmukam śitena cainaṃ bāṇena pratyavidhyat stanāntare
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, laughing, took up another bow and pierced him in return between the breasts with a sharpened arrow.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāsaḥ saṃbhrānta iva saṃyuge bhallena śitadhāreṇa cicchedāsya mahad dhanuḥ
english: That mighty archer, deeply wounded, as if bewildered in the fray, with a keen-edged broad-headed shaft cut asunder his great bow.

sanskrit: yac cāsya bāṇaṃ vikṛtaṃ dhanūṃṣi ca viśāṃ pate sarvaṃ saṃchidya durdharṣo gadāṃ khaḍgam athāpi ca
english: And whatever arrow he sent, and his bows besides, O lord of peoples, the unassailable one cut them all to pieces, and his mace and his sword as well.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tato 'vidhyan navabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ jīvitāntakaraiḥ kruddhaḥ kruddharūpaṃ paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then the scorcher of foes, enraged, pierced the wrathful-looking Dhṛṣṭadyumna with nine keen arrows that bring life to its end.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnarathasyāśvān svarathāśvair mahārathaḥ amiśrayad ameyātmā brāhmam astram udīrayan
english: That great chariot-warrior of measureless soul mingled the horses of Dhṛṣṭadyumna's car with the horses of his own, and loosed the Brāhma weapon.

sanskrit: te miśrā bahv aśobhanta javanā vātaraṃhasaḥ pārāvatasavarṇāś ca śoṇāś ca bharatarṣabha
english: Thus mingled, those swift steeds, fleet as the wind, shone splendidly—some dove-colored, some red, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yathā savidyuto meghā nadanto jaladāgame tathā rejur mahārāja miśritā raṇamūrdhani
english: As thundering clouds charged with lightning at the coming of the rains, so, O great king, they shone, intermingled at the head of the battle.

sanskrit: īṣābandhaṃ cakrabandhaṃ rathabandhaṃ tathaiva ca praṇāśayad ameyātmā dhṛṣṭadyumnasya sa dvijaḥ
english: The pole-fastenings, the wheel-fastenings, and likewise the chariot-fastenings of Dhṛṣṭadyumna's car—all these that brāhmaṇa of measureless soul destroyed.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ uttamām āpadaṃ prāpya gadāṃ vīraḥ parāmṛśat
english: His bow severed, his car broken, his horses slain, his charioteer slain, the hero, fallen into the direst straits, laid hold of his mace.

sanskrit: tām asya viśikhais tīkṣṇaiḥ kṣipyamāṇāṃ mahārathaḥ nijaghāna śarair droṇaḥ kruddhaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
english: As he hurled it, that great chariot-warrior Droṇa, enraged, whose valor was true, struck it down with his keen, barbless arrows.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tu naravyāghro droṇena nihatāṃ śaraiḥ vimalaṃ khaḍgam ādatta śatacandraṃ ca bhānumat
english: Seeing his mace struck down by Droṇa's arrows, that tiger among men took up a spotless sword and a shining shield marked with a hundred moons.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ tathābhūte pāñcālyaḥ sādhv amanyata vadham ācāryamukhyasya prāptakālaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: In such a pass the Pāñcāla prince held, beyond doubt, that the time had surely come for slaying the foremost of teachers, that great-souled one.

sanskrit: tataḥ svarathanīḍasthaḥ svarathasya ratheṣayā agacchad asim udyamya śatacandraṃ ca bhānumat
english: Then, standing in the body of his own car, he advanced along the chariot-pole, raising aloft his sword and the shining shield of a hundred moons.

sanskrit: cikīrṣur duṣkaraṃ karma dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ iyeṣa vakṣo bhettuṃ ca bhāradvājasya saṃyuge
english: Seeking to accomplish a deed hard to do, the great chariot-warrior Dhṛṣṭadyumna desired to cleave the breast of the son of Bharadvāja in the fight.

sanskrit: so 'tiṣṭhad yugamadhye vai yugasaṃnahaneṣu ca śoṇānāṃ jaghanārdheṣu tat sainyāḥ samapūjayan
english: He took his stand in the middle of the yoke, and upon the yoke-fastenings, and upon the hindquarters of the red steeds; and the soldiers honored that feat.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhato yugapālīṣu śoṇān apy adhitiṣṭhataḥ nāpaśyad antaraṃ droṇas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: As he stood upon the yoke-rails and trod even upon the red horses, Droṇa could find no opening in him; and that was as though a marvel.

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ śyenasya carato yathaivāmiṣagṛddhinaḥ tadvad āsīd abhīsāro droṇaṃ prārthayato raṇe
english: Swift as the wheeling of a hawk that hungers for its prey, even so was the onset of him who sought out Droṇa in the battle.

sanskrit: tasyāśvān rathaśaktyāsau tadā kruddhaḥ parākramī sarvān ekaikaśo droṇaḥ kapotābhān ajīghanat
english: Then the enraged and valiant Droṇa, with the spear of his car, slew his horses—all of them, one by one—those steeds dove-gray in hue.

sanskrit: te hatā nyapatan bhūmau dhṛṣṭadyumnasya vājinaḥ śoṇāś ca paryamucyanta rathabandhād viśāṃ pate
english: Slain, the horses of Dhṛṣṭadyumna fell to the earth, and the red steeds were loosed from the chariot-harness, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: tān hayān nihatān dṛṣṭvā dvijāgryeṇa sa pārṣataḥ nāmṛṣyata yudhāṃ śreṣṭho yājñasenir mahārathaḥ
english: Seeing those horses slain by the foremost of brāhmaṇas, the son of Pṛṣata, that best of warriors, the son of Yajñasena, the great chariot-warrior, brooked it not.

sanskrit: virathaḥ sa gṛhītvā tu khaḍgaṃ khaḍgabhṛtāṃ varaḥ droṇam abhyapatad rājan vainateya ivoragam
english: Carless, that best of swordsmen seized his sword and rushed upon Droṇa, O king, as the son of Vinatā swoops upon a serpent.

sanskrit: tasya rūpaṃ babhau rājan bhāradvājaṃ jighāṃsataḥ yathā rūpaṃ paraṃ viṣṇor hiraṇyakaśipor vadhe
english: His form, O king, as he sought to slay the son of Bharadvāja, shone like the supreme form of Viṣṇu in the slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu.

sanskrit: so 'carad vividhān mārgān prakārān ekaviṃśatim bhrāntam udbhrāntam āviddham āplutaṃ prasṛtaṃ sṛtam
english: He moved through manifold paths, the one-and-twenty modes: wheeling, soaring up, weaving, leaping, advancing, gliding,

sanskrit: parivṛttaṃ nivṛttaṃ ca khaḍgaṃ carma ca dhārayan saṃpātaṃ samudīrṇaṃ ca darśayām āsa pārṣataḥ
english: turning about and turning back—and bearing sword and shield, the son of Pṛṣata displayed the swooping strike and the upraised stroke.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasreṇa śatacandram apātayat khaḍgaṃ carma ca saṃbādhe dhṛṣṭadyumnasya sa dvijaḥ
english: Then with a thousand arrows that brāhmaṇa struck down, in the press of battle, the hundred-mooned shield, and the sword and buckler of Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: te tu vaitastikā nāma śarā hy āsannaghātinaḥ nikṛṣṭayuddhe droṇasya nānyeṣāṃ santi te śarāḥ
english: Those arrows, called vaitastika, a span in length, that strike at close quarters in the grappling fight, belonged to Droṇa alone; none others possessed such shafts—

sanskrit: śāradvatasya pārthasya drauṇer vaikartanasya ca pradyumnayuyudhānābhyām abhimanyoś ca te śarāḥ
english: —save for Śāradvata, for Pārtha, for Droṇa's son, and for the son of Vikartana, for Pradyumna and Yuyudhāna, and for Abhimanyu—theirs too were such arrows.

sanskrit: athāsyeṣuṃ samādhatta dṛḍhaṃ paramasaṃśitam antevāsinam ācāryo jighāṃsuḥ putrasaṃmitam
english: Then the teacher fitted to his bow a firm, exceedingly keen arrow, seeking to slay his own pupil, dear to him as a son.

sanskrit: taṃ śarair daśabhis tīkṣṇaiś ciccheda śinipuṃgavaḥ paśyatas tava putrasya karṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ grastam ācāryamukhyena dhṛṣṭadyumnam amocayat
english: That arrow the bull of Śini's line cut through with ten keen shafts, before the very eyes of your son and of the great-souled Karṇa, and freed Dhṛṣṭadyumna, seized by the foremost of teachers.

sanskrit: carantaṃ rathamārgeṣu sātyakiṃ satyavikramam droṇakarṇāntaragataṃ kṛpasyāpi ca bhārata apaśyetāṃ mahātmānau viṣvaksenadhanaṃjayau
english: And Sātyaki of true valor, ranging along the chariot-paths, passing between Droṇa and Karṇa and Kṛpa as well, O Bhārata—him the two great-souled ones, Viṣvaksena and Dhanaṃjaya, beheld.

sanskrit: apūjayetāṃ vārṣṇeyaṃ bruvāṇau sādhu sādhv iti divyāny astrāṇi sarveṣāṃ yudhi nighnantam acyutam abhipatya tataḥ senāṃ viṣvaksenadhanaṃjayau
english: They honored the Vārṣṇeya, crying "Well done! Well done!" as the unfaltering one struck down the celestial weapons of all in the fight; then Viṣvaksena and Dhanaṃjaya fell upon the host.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayas tataḥ kṛṣṇam abravīt paśya keśava ācāryavaramukhyānāṃ madhye krīḍan madhūdvahaḥ
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya said to Kṛṣṇa: "Behold, O Keśava, the scion of the Madhus, sporting in the very midst of the foremost of great teachers!

sanskrit: ānandayati māṃ bhūyaḥ sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ mādrīputrau ca bhīmaṃ ca rājānaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Sātyaki of true valor gladdens me again and again, and the two sons of Mādrī, and Bhīma, and King Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yac chikṣayānuddhataḥ san raṇe carati sātyakiḥ mahārathān upakrīḍan vṛṣṇīnāṃ kīrtivardhanaḥ
english: For by his training Sātyaki, unboastful, ranges through the battle, sporting among the great chariot-warriors—he who magnifies the glory of the Vṛṣṇis."

sanskrit: tam ete pratinandanti siddhāḥ sainyāś ca vismitāḥ ajayyaṃ samare dṛṣṭvā sādhu sādhv iti sātvatam yodhāś cobhayataḥ sarve karmabhiḥ samapūjayan
english: Him the Siddhas and the wondering soldiers acclaimed, beholding the invincible Sātvata in battle, crying "Well done! Well done!"; and the warriors of both sides honored him for his deeds.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca krūram āyodhanaṃ jajñe tasmin rājasamāgame rudrasyeva hi kruddhasya nighnatas tu paśūn yathā
english: Saṃjaya said: A cruel slaughter arose at that gathering of kings, like that of an enraged Rudra striking down the beasts.

sanskrit: hastānām uttamāṅgānāṃ kārmukāṇāṃ ca bhārata chatrāṇāṃ cāpaviddhānāṃ cāmarāṇāṃ ca saṃyuge
english: With severed hands and heads, with bows, O Bhārata, with parasols struck down and with yak-tail whisks in the fray,

sanskrit: bhagnacakrai rathaiś cāpi pātitaiś ca mahādhvajaiḥ sādibhiś ca hataiḥ śūraiḥ saṃkīrṇā vasudhābhavat
english: with broken-wheeled chariots, with great banners cast down, and with slain heroic horsemen, the earth was strewn over.

sanskrit: bāṇapātanikṛttās tu yodhās te kurusattama ceṣṭanto vividhāś ceṣṭā vyadṛśyanta mahāhave
english: The warriors mangled by the fall of arrows, O best of the Kurus, were seen writhing in manifold contortions amid the great battle.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā yuddhe ghore devāsuropame abravīt kṣatriyāṃs tatra dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ abhidravata saṃyattāḥ kumbhayoniṃ mahārathāḥ
english: As the dreadful battle, like that of gods and demons, went on, the Dharma King Yudhiṣṭhira spoke to the kṣatriyas there: "Charge, you great chariot-warriors, girded for the fight, upon the pitcher-born one!

sanskrit: eṣa vai pārṣato vīro bhāradvājena saṃgataḥ ghaṭate ca yathāśakti bhāradvājasya nāśane
english: Here is the heroic son of Pṛṣata, joined in combat with the son of Bharadvāja, striving with all his might at the destruction of the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: yādṛśāni hi rūpāṇi dṛśyante no mahāraṇe adya droṇaṃ raṇe kruddhaḥ pātayiṣyati pārṣataḥ te yūyaṃ sahitā bhūtvā kumbhayoniṃ parīpsata
english: By such portents as we see in this great battle, the son of Pṛṣata, enraged, will today bring Droṇa down in the fight. Be you united, then, and press hard upon the pitcher-born one."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasamājñaptāḥ sṛñjayānāṃ mahārathāḥ abhyadravanta saṃyattā bhāradvājaṃ jighāṃsavaḥ
english: Commanded thus by Yudhiṣṭhira, the great chariot-warriors of the Sṛñjayas, girded for battle, rushed upon the son of Bharadvāja, eager to slay him.

sanskrit: tān samāpatataḥ sarvān bhāradvājo mahārathaḥ abhyadravata vegena martavyam iti niścitaḥ
english: As they all bore down upon him, the great chariot-warrior, the son of Bharadvāja, charged them with speed, resolved that he must die.

sanskrit: prayāte satyasaṃdhe tu samakampata medinī vavur vātāḥ sanirghātās trāsayanto varūthinīm
english: When the one true to his vow set forth, the earth trembled, and winds blew with crashing thunderclaps, striking terror into the host.

sanskrit: papāta mahatī colkā ādityān nirgateva ha dīpayantīva tāpena śaṃsantīva mahad bhayam
english: And a great meteor fell, as if it had issued from the sun, seeming to set all aflame with its heat, seeming to portend some mighty terror.

sanskrit: jajvaluś caiva śastrāṇi bhāradvājasya māriṣa rathāḥ svananti cātyarthaṃ hayāś cāśrūṇy avāsṛjan
english: The weapons of the son of Bharadvāja blazed up, O honored one, his chariots groaned exceedingly, and his horses let fall their tears.

sanskrit: hataujā iva cāpy āsīd bhāradvājo mahārathaḥ ṛṣīṇāṃ brahmavādānāṃ svargasya gamanaṃ prati suyuddhena tataḥ prāṇān utsraṣṭum upacakrame
english: The great chariot-warrior, the son of Bharadvāja, seemed as one whose vigor had been struck away; and resolving upon the heaven-bound path of the seers who proclaim the Veda, he began, through a worthy fight, to give up his life-breaths.

sanskrit: tataś caturdiśaṃ sainyair drupadasyābhisaṃvṛtaḥ nirdahan kṣatriyavrātān droṇaḥ paryacarad raṇe
english: Then, hemmed in on all four sides by Drupada's troops, Droṇa ranged through the battle, consuming the hosts of kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: hatvā viṃśatisāhasrān kṣatriyān arimardanaḥ daśāyutāni tīkṣṇāgrair avadhīd viśikhaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: The crusher of foes, having slain twenty thousand kṣatriyas, slew a hundred thousand more with his keen, sharp-pointed barbless shafts.

sanskrit: so 'tiṣṭhad āhave yatto vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ kṣatriyāṇām abhāvāya brāhmam ātmānam āsthitaḥ
english: He stood firm in the battle, intent, like a smokeless fire, set upon the destruction of the kṣatriyas, having assumed the form of Brahman within himself.

sanskrit: pāñcālyaṃ virathaṃ bhīmo hatasarvāyudhaṃ vaśī aviṣaṇṇaṃ mahātmānaṃ tvaramāṇaḥ samabhyayāt
english: The self-controlled Bhīma hastened toward the Pāñcāla prince, carless, stripped of all his weapons, yet unflinching and great of soul.

sanskrit: tataḥ svaratham āropya pāñcālyam arimardanaḥ abravīd abhisaṃprekṣya droṇam asyantam antikāt
english: Then the crusher of foes, taking the Pāñcāla up onto his own car, looked upon Droṇa loosing his shafts close at hand, and spoke:

sanskrit: na tvad anya ihācāryaṃ yoddhum utsahate pumān tvarasva prāgvadhāyaiva tvayi bhāraḥ samāhitaḥ
english: "No other man than you here dares to fight the teacher. Make haste to his slaying; upon you the burden is laid."

sanskrit: sa tathokto mahābāhuḥ sarvabhārasahaṃ navam abhipatyādade kṣipram āyudhapravaraṃ dṛḍham
english: Thus addressed, the mighty-armed one swiftly seized a fresh and firm weapon, the choicest of arms, able to bear every strain.

sanskrit: saṃrabdhaś ca śarān asyan droṇaṃ durvāraṇaṃ raṇe vivārayiṣur ācāryaṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: And in fury, loosing his arrows, eager to hold back the teacher Droṇa, hard to ward off in battle, he overwhelmed him with showers of shafts.

sanskrit: tau nyavārayatāṃ śreṣṭhau saṃrabdhau raṇaśobhinau udīrayetāṃ brāhmāṇi divyāny astrāṇy anekaśaḥ
english: Those two foremost warriors, wrathful, the glory of the battlefield, held each other in check, and again and again loosed celestial weapons sprung from Brahmā.

sanskrit: sa mahāstrair mahārāja droṇam ācchādayad raṇe nihatya sarvāṇy astrāṇi bhāradvājasya pārṣataḥ
english: With his mighty weapons, O great king, the son of Pṛṣata enveloped Droṇa in the battle, having quelled all the weapons of the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: sa vasātīñ śibīṃś caiva bāhlīkān kauravān api rakṣiṣyamāṇān saṃgrāme droṇaṃ vyadhamad acyutaḥ
english: And the unfaltering one scattered the Vasātis and the Śibis, the Bāhlīkas and the Kauravas too, as they sought to shield Droṇa in the fray.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tadā rājan gabhastibhir ivāṃśumān babhau pracchādayann āśāḥ śarajālaiḥ samantataḥ
english: Then Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O king, shone like the sun with its rays, veiling all the quarters about him with nets of arrows on every side.

sanskrit: tasya droṇo dhanuś chittvā viddhvā cainaṃ śilīmukhaiḥ marmāṇy abhyahanad bhūyaḥ sa vyathāṃ paramām agāt
english: Droṇa cut through his bow and, piercing him with stone-headed arrows, struck again at his vital parts; and he came to the utmost anguish.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo dṛḍhakrodho droṇasyāśliṣya taṃ ratham śanakair iva rājendra droṇaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Bhīma, his wrath grown firm, gripping that chariot of Droṇa's, spoke to Droṇa, O lord of kings, slowly and deliberately:

sanskrit: yadi nāma na yudhyerañ śikṣitā brahmabandhavaḥ svakarmabhir asaṃtuṣṭā na sma kṣatraṃ kṣayaṃ vrajet
english: "If only these so-called brāhmaṇas, trained for war yet unsatisfied with their own proper duties, did not fight, the kṣatriya order would not be going to ruin.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā sarvabhūteṣu dharmaṃ jyāyastaraṃ viduḥ tasya ca brāhmaṇo mūlaṃ bhavāṃś ca brahmavittamaḥ
english: Harmlessness toward all beings the wise hold to be the higher law, and of that law the brāhmaṇa is the root—and you are the foremost knower of the Veda.

sanskrit: śvapākavan mlecchagaṇān hatvā cānyān pṛthagvidhān ajñānān mūḍhavad brahman putradāradhanepsayā
english: Like an outcaste dog-cooker, O brāhmaṇa, slaying hordes of barbarians and others of every sort, ignorant men, as a deluded creature might, out of craving for son and wife and wealth—

sanskrit: ekasyārthe bahūn hatvā putrasyādharmavid yathā svakarmasthān vikarmastho na vyapatrapase katham
english: —for the sake of one, your son, slaying many, like one heedless of dharma, you who have strayed from your own calling slay those who keep to theirs: how is it you feel no shame?

sanskrit: sa cādya patitaḥ śete pṛṣṭenāveditas tava dharmarājena tad vākyaṃ nātiśaṅkitum arhasi
english: And he today lies fallen, as the Dharma King declared to you when you asked. That word you ought not to doubt overmuch."

sanskrit: evam uktas tato droṇo bhīmenotsṛjya tad dhanuḥ sarvāṇy astrāṇi dharmātmā hātukāmo 'bhyabhāṣata karṇa karṇa maheṣvāsa kṛpa duryodhaneti ca
english: Thus addressed by Bhīma, the righteous-souled Droṇa, wishing to cast away that bow and all his weapons, spoke: "Karṇa, Karṇa, great archer! Kṛpa! Duryodhana!

sanskrit: saṃgrāme kriyatāṃ yatno bravīmy eṣa punaḥ punaḥ pāṇḍavebhyaḥ śivaṃ vo 'stu śastram abhyutsṛjāmy aham
english: Let your utmost effort be made in the battle—this I tell you again and again. Against the Pāṇḍavas may all go well with you. I am laying down my arms."

sanskrit: iti tatra mahārāja prākrośad drauṇim eva ca utsṛjya ca raṇe śastraṃ rathopasthe niveśya ca abhayaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ pradadau yogayuktavān
english: Thus, O great king, he cried out there, and to Droṇa's son as well; and casting away his weapon in the battle and seating himself upon the body of the car, the one yoked in yoga granted safety to all beings.
